One shared query can serve several targets, but acquiring facts does not guarantee useful future predictions. This selection costs one model call plus its measured tokens and compute. forecast_executor_kind identifies the forecast executor: program forecasts consume zero model calls and tokens; llm forecasts consume one model call plus tokens. forecast_model_call_cost states that per-forecast call charge explicitly, and forecast_call_upper states the required resource reservation, including compute for either executor. All charges use the same session budgets. The remaining hard resources shown exclude this selection's reservation. Consider remaining calendar ticks and all scored opportunities, including those left at their baseline. Each target's current_state shows whether it already has an explicit override. The session protocol controls whether a relevant baseline change invalidates that override (base_bound_override) or retains it (persistent_override). Choose zero or more registered query handles and zero or more forecast handles, up to the stated capacity. You may save resources. Use only the public common inputs and lawfully acquired shared reports shown here. Return only JSON: {"query_order":["q0"],"forecast_handles":["t0"]}. Handles must be unique and registered; no extra prose.
